Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X66/X66n1296.xml). The cited Chan collection records that The cited Chan collection records that The cited Chan collection records that The cited Chan collection records that Collected Raising of Old Cases of the School: The commentator Gunanmen explicitly appraises both Bensheng and Xuedou Chongxian as genuine adepts and masters, then faults their elaborate efforts against the unnamed monk’s single cutting-off response.

Senses.Explanation: A genuine adept and master of the school is a public appraisal of someone whose handling of an encounter withstands immediate scrutiny. The expression is often spoken by the person being tested, not claimed by the praised respondent. An explicitly unnamed questioner applies it to Kaixian Shanxian, who answers that someone will know thirty years later; another explicitly unnamed questioner applies it to Huanglong Huinan, who responds with a shout; Yulin Tongxiu raises his staff when an interlocutor offers the same praise. Later commentators also use it as a verdict. Xuedou Chongxian says an articulate monk has exhausted bow and arrows and does not equal Bensheng as a genuine adept and master of the school. Yuanwu Keqin compares such an adept to a bright mirror: the foreigner comes and a foreigner appears, the Han person comes and a Han person appears. This is an attested description of responsive encounter conduct, not an imported rank or mystical attainment. Two lamp compilations preserve the Kaixian exchange. Their agreement shows circulation of the case but does not count as two different encounter shapes; the other four works supply independent appraisal and commentary contexts.
